audience: Finance and credit-control staff who set up customer payment reminders and then chase overdue customers every day.
goal: Set up a **ladder of follow-up levels** (a reminder after 15 days, a letter after 30, a final notice after 60), then use the **Follow-up Reports** worklist to review customers, open a customer's follow-up, prepare a reminder in the **Send and Print** window, and understand how to remind many customers at once.
before: You can open the **Accounting** app, including **Configuration** and **Customers**.
Decide how many reminder stages you want and after how many days each one starts. This guide uses **15, 30 and 60** days.
For SMS, the customer needs a mobile number and your database needs SMS credits. For e-mail, the customer needs an e-mail address.
outcome: Three follow-up levels exist: a 1st reminder by e-mail, a 2nd reminder by letter, and a final notice by SMS with a call to the credit controller.
You know how to read the **Follow-up Reports** worklist and open one customer's follow-up.
You have seen the **Send and Print** window and know where to send a reminder, and where to process reminders in bulk.
notes: The screenshots were captured by an automated run on a **test database**. The red banner at the top ("Database neutralized for testing") only appears on test databases, and no e-mails are sent from it.

**Each number of days can be used by one level only** (per company). On the test database the 15, 30 and 60 day levels already existed, so the automated run created its three levels as **[TEST]** levels with **115, 130 and 160** days and deleted them afterwards. Your own levels use the days you choose, such as 15, 30 and 60.
When **Schedule Activity** is ticked, **Activity Type** and **Summary** are required. Odoo will not save the level until both are filled in.

The automated run only **looks at** the daily-routine screens. It does not change a customer, does not press **Send**, and does not run **Process Automatic Follow-ups**, because those actions send real reminders.
If a customer has no e-mail address, Odoo opens an extra **Edit: customer** window on top of Send and Print. Add the address, or discard the window, before you continue.

phases.title: Open the Follow-up Levels list
phases.summary: Go from the Accounting app to the list of reminder stages.
phases.checkpoint: A blank **follow-up level** form is open, ready to fill in.

phases.title: Create the 1st reminder (e-mail)
phases.summary: Name the stage, set its delay and choose how it contacts the customer.
phases.checkpoint: The **1st reminder** is saved: e-mail, automatic, invoices attached, with an activity scheduled.

phases.title: Create the 2nd reminder (letter)
phases.summary: Add a stage that also prints a letter.
phases.checkpoint: The **2nd reminder** is saved with a longer delay and **Send a Letter** ticked.

phases.title: Create the final notice and review the ladder
phases.summary: Add the SMS stage with a call activity, then look at all stages together.
phases.checkpoint: The list shows your three stages in order of days.

phases.title: Open the Follow-up Reports worklist
phases.summary: Switch from set-up to the daily routine.
phases.checkpoint: The **Follow-up Reports** list shows one line per customer with money outstanding.

phases.title: Review one customer
phases.summary: Open a customer's follow-up and read what it offers.
phases.checkpoint: You know where the stage bar, the exclude switch, the Automatic/Manual setting and the next reminder date are.

phases.title: Prepare a reminder
phases.summary: Open the Send and Print window, check its content, then close it without sending.
phases.checkpoint: The window is closed and **nothing was sent**.

phases.title: Remind many customers at once
phases.summary: Select customers and find the bulk action.
phases.checkpoint: You have found **Process Automatic Follow-ups** in the Actions menu.

glossary.meaning: One reminder stage, such as "1st reminder after 15 days". The levels form a ladder a customer climbs as an invoice stays unpaid.
How many days **after the invoice due date** a level starts. Each number of days can be used only once per company.
Odoo sends this level by itself when the delay is reached. Without it, Finance reviews and sends each reminder.
Adds the overdue invoices, as PDFs, to the reminder.
Also creates a to-do (for example a call) for the credit controller each time the level is reached.
Whether the customer needs action today (**In need of action**) or is waiting for the next reminder date.
The date the customer comes back onto the worklist.
The window where you choose how a reminder is delivered (Print, Email, SMS, By post) and check its wording before sending.

1.title: Open the Accounting app
1.do: On the Odoo home screen, click the **Accounting** app.
actions: Go to the Odoo home screen.
1.see: The Accounting app opens with its menu bar across the top.
1.why: Customer follow-ups are part of the Accounting app.

2.title: Open the Configuration menu
2.do: In the top menu bar, click **Configuration**.
actions: Look at the menu bar across the top.
2.see: A drop-down with the Accounting settings and set-up lists.
2.why: Reminder stages are set up first, before any customer is chased.
2.tip: If **Configuration** is missing, widen the browser window; narrow windows hide menu entries behind a **+**.

3.title: Open Follow-up Levels
3.where: Accounting app > Configuration > Invoicing > Follow-up Levels
actions: Find the **Invoicing** group in the drop-down.
Wait for the list to load.
3.see: The **Follow-up Levels** list with its columns: Description, Due Days, Send Email, Send SMS Message, Send a Letter, Automatic, Activity and Company.
3.why: These levels are the stages Odoo walks a customer through as an invoice gets older. The list may already contain levels; each one needs its own number of days.

4.title: Create a new follow-up level
4.do: Click the purple **New** button at the top left.
actions: Find the **New** button next to the title.
4.see: An empty follow-up level form with a **Notification** tab and an **Activity** tab.
4.why: Each reminder stage is its own record, so you add one level per stage.

5.title: Name the first stage
5.do: Type a clear name in the **Description** field.
actions: Click the large **Description** field at the top of the form.
5.see: The name appears in large letters at the top of the form.
5.why: This name is what staff see on every customer's follow-up, so make it say what the stage does.
5.tip: Put the channel in the name, such as "Email" or "Letter", so the ladder is easy to read.

6.title: Set the delay in days
6.do: Next to **Remind**, enter how many days after the due date this stage starts.
6.where: Follow-up level form > Remind … days after due date
6.see: The line reads **Remind 15 days after due date**.
6.why: A customer reaches this stage once an invoice is this many days past its due date.
6.warning: Every level needs a **different** number of days. If another level already uses the number, Odoo refuses to save with *Days of the follow-up lines must be different per company*.

7.title: Choose the actions
7.do: Under **Notification**, make sure **Send Email** is ticked.
7.where: Follow-up level form > Notification tab > Send Email
actions: Tick it if it is not already ticked.
7.see: **Send Email** is ticked. **Send a Letter** and **Send SMS Message** can be added too.
7.why: The ticked actions decide how the customer is contacted at this stage.

8.title: Content Template (optional)
8.do: Look at the **Content Template** field and leave it empty.
8.where: Follow-up level form > Notification tab > Content Template
actions: Leave it empty to use Odoo's standard wording.
Choose an e-mail template only if you want a specific message for this stage.
8.see: The field is empty, so the standard follow-up wording is used.
8.why: A template lets each stage use its own message, for example firmer wording at later stages.

9.title: Tick Automatic
9.where: Follow-up level form > Notification tab > Automatic
9.why: With Automatic on, Odoo sends this stage by itself when the delay is reached. Leave it off if Finance wants to check each reminder first.
9.tip: Use Automatic for gentle early reminders and keep later, firmer stages manual.

10.title: Keep Attach Invoices ticked
10.where: Follow-up level form > Notification tab > Attach Invoices
actions: Check it is ticked; tick it if not.
10.why: The overdue invoice PDFs travel with the reminder, and customers settle faster when the invoice is in front of them.

11.title: Open the Activity tab
actions: Find the two tabs above the form: **Notification** and **Activity**.
11.see: The Activity tab with **Schedule Activity**, **Responsible**, **Activity Type** and **Summary**.
11.why: Here you can also create an internal task for the credit controller when this stage is reached.

12.title: Schedule an activity
12.do: Tick **Schedule Activity**, then fill in **Activity Type** and **Summary**.
12.where: Follow-up level form > Activity tab > Schedule Activity
actions: Type a **Summary**, for example **Review overdue balance**.
12.see: **Schedule Activity** is ticked and both **Activity Type** and **Summary** are filled in.
12.why: Each time a customer reaches this stage, Odoo creates this activity for the responsible user.
12.warning: Once **Schedule Activity** is ticked, **Activity Type** and **Summary** are required. The level cannot be saved while either is empty.
12.tip: This is optional. Leave it off for a purely automatic e-mail stage.

13.title: Save the first stage
13.do: Click the **cloud icon** (Save manually) at the top left.
actions: Look next to the record name at the top left.
13.see: The cloud icon disappears: the level is saved.
13.why: Nothing is stored until you save. The first stage is now live.
13.warning: If an error says days must be different, another level already uses that number of days. Change the number and save again.

14.title: Add the second stage
actions: Click the **New** button at the top left.
14.why: There is one level per escalation step. The order is driven purely by the number of days.

15.title: Name the second stage
15.see: The name appears at the top of the form.
15.why: This stage escalates from an e-mail to a printed letter.

16.title: Set the second delay
16.where: Follow-up level form > Remind … days after due date
16.see: The line reads **Remind 30 days after due date**.
16.why: Each stage must have a longer delay than the one before it, so customers move up the ladder as time passes.

17.title: Go to the Notification tab
actions: Look at the tabs above the form.
17.see: The Notification tab with **Send Email**, **Send SMS Message**, **Send a Letter** and **Automatic**.
17.why: This is where you choose how this stage contacts the customer.

18.title: Tick Send a Letter
18.where: Follow-up level form > Notification tab > Send a Letter
18.why: At 30 days overdue the customer receives a printed reminder as well as the e-mail.

19.title: Save the second stage
actions: Click the **cloud** icon at the top left.
19.why: **Automatic** was left off here, so Finance reviews the 30-day letter before it goes out.

20.title: Add the final stage
actions: Click the **New** button at the top left.
20.why: The third level is the final notice.

21.title: Name the final stage
21.see: The name appears at the top of the form.
21.why: The name says what this stage does: an SMS and a call.

22.title: Set the final delay
22.where: Follow-up level form > Remind … days after due date
22.see: The line reads **Remind 60 days after due date**.
22.why: Anything still unpaid 60 days past due reaches the last stage and stays there.

23.title: Tick Send SMS Message
23.where: Follow-up level form > Notification tab > Send SMS Message
23.why: An SMS gets the customer's attention at the last stage.
23.warning: SMS needs credits and a mobile number on the customer record.

24.title: Open the Activity tab
24.why: For the final notice you also raise an internal task.

25.title: Tick Schedule Activity
25.where: Follow-up level form > Activity tab > Schedule Activity
25.see: The **Activity Type** and **Summary** fields are now required.
25.why: A call is logged for the credit controller each time a customer reaches this stage.

26.title: Choose the Activity Type and Summary
26.do: Choose **Call** as the **Activity Type** and type a **Summary**.
26.where: Follow-up level form > Activity tab > Activity Type
actions: Type a **Summary**, for example **Call customer - final notice**.
26.why: Odoo creates this activity on the customer when the stage is reached. **Responsible** defaults to the follow-up responsible.

27.title: Save the final stage
actions: Click the **cloud** icon at the top left.
27.why: The three stages are now in place: e-mail, then letter, then SMS plus a call.

28.title: Review the stages
28.do: Click the **Follow-up Levels** breadcrumb to see all stages.
28.where: Follow-up level form > Follow-up Levels breadcrumb
actions: Click **Follow-up Levels** at the top left.
Read down the list, in order of days.
points: **Due Days** shows when each stage starts.
The ticks show how each stage contacts the customer.
**Activity** shows the task type, if any.
28.see: The list shows every stage with its days and channels.
28.why: Set-up is finished. The rest of the guide is the day-to-day work.
28.tip: Check that the days increase from stage to stage.

29.title: Open the Customers menu
29.do: In the top menu bar, click **Customers**.
actions: Look at the menu bar across the top.
29.see: A drop-down with the customer entries, including **Follow-up Reports**.
29.why: The daily routine starts from the Customers menu.

30.title: Open Follow-up Reports
actions: Wait for the list to load.
30.see: The **Follow-up Reports** list, with an **Overdue Invoices** filter already applied.
30.why: This is the credit-control worklist: one line per customer with money outstanding.

31.title: Read the worklist
31.do: Read the **Follow-up Status** and **Follow-up Level** columns.
actions: Look at **Next reminder**, **Total Due** and **Total Overdue**.
points: **Follow-up Status** shows who needs chasing today.
**Follow-up Level** shows which stage each customer has reached.
**Next reminder** is the date the next stage is due.
31.see: One line per customer, with a status badge such as **In need of action**.
31.why: This list tells you who to chase and how far each customer has already climbed the ladder.

32.title: Open a customer's follow-up
32.do: Click a customer's line to open their follow-up report.
actions: Find the customer in the list (the guide uses **Test Credit Customer**).
32.see: The customer's follow-up page, with the **Follow up** button, the overdue invoices and the chatter on the right.
32.why: Any line on the list works the same way.

33.title: Read the stage bar
33.do: Look at the **stage bar** to see where the customer stands.
actions: Look for the bar of stages near the top.
33.see: The stages you configured, with the customer's current stage highlighted.
33.why: Clicking a stage on this bar moves the customer to it by hand.
33.tip: Look, but do not click a stage unless you really want to move the customer.

34.title: Exclude a line from follow-ups
34.do: Find the **Exclude from Follow-ups** column on the invoice lines.
34.where: Customer follow-up > invoice lines > Exclude from Follow-ups
actions: Find the exclude switch at the end of each line.
34.why: Switch it on for a line that is disputed, already paid or under a payment plan. Excluded lines are ignored when the stage is calculated.

35.title: Automatic or Manual reminders
35.see: The setting shows **Automatic** for this customer.
35.why: Automatic lets Odoo follow the stage schedule. Switch to **Manual** for a customer you want to chase by hand, such as a key account under negotiation.

36.title: Check the next reminder date
36.do: Find **Next reminder** on the customer's page.
36.see: The date the customer comes back onto the worklist.
36.why: Push the date forward if the customer has promised to pay by a certain day.
36.tip: The guide only looks at this field; it changes nothing.

37.title: Click Follow up
actions: Find the **Follow up** button at the top left.
Wait for the window to open.
37.why: This is where you choose how this reminder reaches the customer.
37.warning: If the customer has no e-mail address, a second window **Edit: customer** opens on top. Add the address, or discard that window, before continuing.

38.title: Choose the send channels
38.do: Look at the **Actions** ticks at the top of the window.
38.see: **Email** is ticked, taken from the stage the customer is on.
38.why: The ticks are pre-set from the customer's stage. Tick **Print** for a hard copy, **Sms** for a text, or **By post** to send it through the postal service.

39.title: Check the message
actions: Read the subject and the body of the message.
39.see: A ready-made reminder addressed to the customer.
39.why: The body comes from the stage's template. Edit it for a one-off note, for example to mention a cheque the customer says they posted. The overdue table is added automatically.

40.title: Attach the invoices
40.why: The overdue invoice PDFs travel with the reminder. Use **Attachment** to add anything else, such as a signed delivery note.

41.title: Find the Send button
41.do: Find the **Send** button at the bottom of the window. Do not click it.
actions: Look at the bottom of the window.
Find **Send** (the label changes to **Send & Print** when Print is ticked).
41.why: In daily use, **Send** dispatches the reminder, logs it in the chatter and moves the customer to the next stage.
41.warning: **Send** sends the reminder for real. Only press it when you mean it.

42.title: Close the window
42.do: Click **Cancel** to close the window without sending.
actions: Click **Cancel** at the bottom of the window.
42.see: The window closes and the customer's page is shown again.
42.why: Nothing is dispatched and the customer stays on the same stage.

43.title: Back to the worklist
actions: Click **Follow-up Reports** at the top left.
43.why: Reminders can also be sent to many customers at once.

44.title: Select customers
44.do: Tick the box in the list header to select every customer on the page.
actions: Find the empty box at the top-left of the list.
44.see: Every line is ticked and the header shows **20 selected**.
44.why: This is how the monthly reminder run is done. You can also tick individual rows.
44.warning: Check how many customers are selected before you run an action on them.

45.title: Open the Actions menu
45.do: Click **Actions** at the top of the list.
actions: Find the **Actions** button next to the selection counter.
45.see: A menu with Export, Archive, Merge, Send email, Send SMS Text Message, **Process Automatic Follow-ups** and more.
45.why: With customers selected, these actions work on the whole batch.

46.title: Process Automatic Follow-ups
46.do: Find **Process Automatic Follow-ups** in the menu.
46.where: Follow-up Reports > Actions > Process Automatic Follow-ups
actions: Click it only when you want every due reminder sent.
46.see: The menu entry that sends every due reminder for the selected customers in one run.
46.why: It uses each customer's own stage. **Send email** and **Send SMS Text Message** above it are the manual bulk alternatives.
46.warning: This sends real reminders to every selected customer. The automated test points at it but never clicks it.
46.tip: That completes the tour: set up the ladder, review customers, prepare a reminder and process a batch.
